newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba campaigns against US move to tighten embargo.
newsitem.headline: Cuba campaigns against US move to tighten embargo.

text.p: Cuba has sent envoys to 18 countries this month seeking help in opposing moves in the U.S. Congress to toughen the economic embargo the United States imposed on the island 35 years ago.
The ruling Communist Party newspaper Granma said on Tuesday that President Fidel Castro's government had moved against "new campaigns and conspiracies by the United States."

The diplomatic offensive is aimed at countering a series of amendments to a foreign policy bill currently moving through Congress that would toughen the Helms-Burton law and other aspects of the U.S. embargo against Cuba.

Since the start of this month, Granma said, Deputy President Carlos Lage had visited Uruguay, Argentina, Chile and Brazil, presenting a letter from Castro to leaders of those countries denouncing the U.S. moves.

Parliamentary President Ricardo Alarcon visited Colombia and Venezuela on a similar mission while Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina went to El Salvador, Mexico, Honduras, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Panama, the Dominican Republic and Nicaragua.

Deputy foreign ministers Jorge Bolanos and Isabel Allende went to Canada, the Vatican, the World Trade Organisation in Geneva, the European Union in Brussels and the Netherlands, which currently holds the rotating EU presidency.

Cuba's campaign has sought to revive opposition to the Helms-Burton law, which was criticised from the outset by U.S. allies because it includes provisions to punish third country firms investing in property expropriated from U.S. firms and citizens after Castro's 1959 revolution.

Washington's current stance is that tensions over the law have eased and that, even if there are still differences of opinion over tactics towards Havana, allies are increasingly joining it in pressing Cuba to adopt political reforms.
